editorial:
Imagine being so obsessed with money that you would do anything to get it. That is exactly where you find Jonathan Corliss. He is a smart college student who treats people like stepping stones. He dates a rich girl named Dorothy just to get close to her wealthy father. But when a pregnancy threatens his plan to get rich, he does something terrible and tries to make it look like she took her own life. The vibe is tense and sneaky, making you feel like you are watching a predator play a dangerous game of chess.

You will love how the tension builds when Dorothy's twin sister, Ellen, enters the picture. She does not believe her sister just gave up on life, and watching her hunt for the truth is the best part of the film. The acting is solid and the twists keep you guessing. While it moves a bit slow in the middle, the payoff is worth it. It is a great pick for a rainy weekend night.
endingExplained: Everything falls apart for Jonathan when Ellen finally proves he is a killer. In the final scenes, the truth comes out and Jonathan realizes he cannot manipulate his way out of this one. He ends up meeting a brutal end, proving that his greed was his downfall. The movie wraps up with the bad guy getting exactly what he deserves, leaving you feeling satisfied that the truth finally won.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological games and crime mysteries.
